claims.text_en: The app's scored unit 'st.sena-ruam' is anchored on a point where no operating BTS station exists. Its center (13.78594, 100.54686) sits on Phahonyothin Road roughly midway between BTS Ari (734 m south-west) and BTS Saphan Khwai (929 m north-east), and OSM records no rail station at or near that point. The name corresponds to สถานีเสนาร่วม (Sena Ruam), a BTS Sukhumvit Line infill station with reserved code N6 planned between Ari (N5) and Saphan Khwai (N7) that has never been built; the app's rail.json nonetheless lists it as an operating bts_sukhumvit station, and the area's app-defined neighbours are 'ari' and 'saphan-khwai'.

geography.notes: Center point and neighbours from app snapshot bkk-d6499618507e7561; distances computed between OSM station nodes and the app point.

temporal_scope.observed_period: stable since the app snapshot (2026-10); the underlying planning history is stable since 1999
temporal_scope.notes: Identity check required by the brief: the brief's premise of an operating northern-extension station at these coordinates is contradicted by both app internals and OSM.

evidence.locator: Overpass query 1 — railway=station within 3500 m of 13.78594,100.54686 (20 hits)
evidence.paraphrase: The station list around the app point includes Ari (13.77971, 100.54462), Saphan Khwai (13.79382, 100.54971) and Mo Chit (13.8026, 100.55379) but nothing within about 700 m of the app center; app and OSM coordinates for Ari, Saphan Khwai and Mo Chit match to 5 decimal places.

rail.json lists 'Sena Ruam' at 13.78594, 100.54686 with lines ['bts_sukhumvit'] as if operating; the scored area's neighbours are 'ari' and 'saphan-khwai'.

limitations: The app snapshot is internal project data, not an external source; its presentation as an operating station is reported here as app behaviour, verified against OSM.
OSM coverage of railways is generally strong in Bangkok, but absence of a station node is a negative claim from mapping data.

claims.text_en: The planned station's published siting matches the unit's center: Thai Wikipedia places สถานีเสนาร่วม (N6) elevated over Phahonyothin Road at the mouth of Soi Phahonyothin 9 (Soi Si Fa), in front of Prasanmit Hospital and the ESV building, in Khwaeng Sam Sen Nai, Phaya Thai district — quoting its lead: 'จะยกระดับเหนือถนนพหลโยธิน ปากซอยพหลโยธิน 9 (ซอยสีฟ้า) ในพื้นที่เขตพญาไท'. The same page's infobox calls it a future station with construction expected from 2026 and service targeted for 5 December 2032, while its History section records the project as cancelled with completed designs to be transferred to the BMA as the concession ends (2029).

geography.notes: The siting point (Soi Phahonyothin 9 mouth) lies within 300 m of the app's center point — OSM maps Soi Phahonyothin 9 ways within 280 m of the center.

temporal_scope.notes: Status is contested between the page's own infobox (start 2026, service 2032) and its history section (cancelled); the Prachachat hearing (c03) is the fresher statement.

evidence.locator: Lead + ที่ตั้ง section + infobox + History section
evidence.paraphrase: Verbatim Thai: lead places the station over Phahonyothin at the mouth of Soi Phahonyothin 9 (Soi Si Fa) in Phaya Thai; the location section names โรงพยาบาลประสานมิตร, the ESV building, AIS Tower 2 and Khwaeng Sam Sen Nai; infobox marks 'สถานีในอนาคต' with construction expected 2569 BE and service 5 ธ.ค. 2575 BE; history says the project was cancelled and designs go to BMA.

evidence.paraphrase: OSM shows Soi Phahonyothin 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and Soi Sena Ruam ways around the center, consistent with the planned station's soi-9 siting.

limitations: Thai Wikipedia's own cited sources for the article are 2018-2020 vintage; the 2026 construction-start expectation is unverified by news.

claims.text_en: As of November 2026 the station remains unbuilt and politically live: on 4 November 2026 Phaya Thai Metropolitan Council member Worawit Chaisuwan asked the BMA why Sena Ruam (N6) — in the plan since 1999 — has never progressed, and why the operator's fare table still includes the unbuilt station; he cited the 1.6 km Saphan Khwai-Ari hop costing 25 baht, more than longer extension segments, describing fares as inflated by the missing station. Deputy governor Wisanu Trepsupol replied that N6 was not directly in the original concession (which required at least 17 stations; 24 are now open including Saint Louis), that BMA sees it as important and will coordinate with agencies ahead of the concession's expiry in 2029, and that fare unification under MRTA single ownership would resolve the anomaly. No construction schedule was committed.

geography.notes: The fare anomaly applies to exactly the unit's gap: Ari-Saphan Khwai.

temporal_scope.observed_period: Council question of 4 Nov 2026; planning record since 1999
temporal_scope.notes: Strongest current counter-evidence for the transport and rent readings of this unit; directly on the scored gap.

evidence.locator: Article body — council question and deputy governor's reply
evidence.paraphrase: Prachachat (5 Nov 2026) reports councilor Worawit Chaisuwan pressing BMA on building N6 ('บรรจุในแผนมาตั้งแต่ปี 2542 แต่ยังไม่เกิดขึ้นจริง') and on fares including the unbuilt station, with the Saphan Khwai-Ari 1.6 km hop at 25 baht; Wisanu says N6 was not directly in the concession, BMA will coordinate, concession ends 2572 BE (2029).

limitations: Single-outlet report; no independent second news account of the hearing was found in this session.
The fare figure is quoted from the councilor's statement, not from a fare table.

claims.text_en: The operating Sukhumvit Line stations north of the unit opened in phases and none is named 'Sena Ruam': Ha Yaek Lat Phrao (N9) opened 9 August 2019 as the northern terminus; Phahonyothin 24 (N10), Ratchayothin (N11), Sena Nikhom (N12) and Kasetsart University (N13) opened together on 4 December 2019 (Kasetsart University then became the terminus); four further stations toward Wat Phra Si Mahathat opened 5 June 2020; and terminus Khu Khot opened 16 December 2020. The extension station most likely confused with 'Sena Ruam' is Sena Nikhom (N12), which the app's own rail.json carries as 'sena-nikhom' — about 6.3 km north-east of the app's sena-ruam point.

geography.notes: The extension corridor runs 4.7-11 km north of the unit along Phahonyothin; the brief's hypothesised clipping stations 'phahonyothin-24' and 'kasetsart-university' exist as app areas but sit 4,742 m and 7,068 m away and do not clip this cell.

temporal_scope.notes: Answers the brief's 'verify exact date for Sena Ruam': there is no such operating station to date; the phased opening is 2019-2020, and no phase date attaches to a 'Sena Ruam'.

evidence.locator: Opening date and 'northern terminus until 4 December 2019' lines
evidence.paraphrase: English Wikipedia: Ha Yaek Lat Phrao (N9) opened 9 August 2019 and remained the northern terminus until Kasetsart University station opened on 4 December 2019.

Sena Nikhom (N12) opened 4 December 2019, having been requested to open with the Ha Yaek Lat Phrao-Kasetsart University phase in December 2019; neighbours Ratchayothin (south) and Kasetsart University (north).
Kasetsart University (N13) opened 4 December 2019; four more stations toward Wat Phra Si Mahathat opened 5 June 2020.
Khu Khot began service 16 December 2020 as the terminus of the 19 km Mo Chit-Saphan Mai-Khu Khot extension.
App rail coordinates place sena-nikhom 6,313 m from the app's sena-ruam point, phahonyothin-24 4,742 m, kasetsart-university 7,068 m.

limitations: Ratchayothin (N11) and Phahonyothin 24 (N10) opening dates are carried by the 4 December 2019 phase rather than by dedicated page reads this session.
The 5 June 2020 'four more stations' figure comes from one Wikipedia page; segment-by-segment dating was not independently confirmed.

claims.text_en: The scored polygon is a 10-vertex cell of about 1.25 km² (app fact: 1.26) spanning lat 13.78068-13.79184, lng 100.53953-100.55426 — consistent with an 800 m circle around the center clipped north and south by the Voronoi cells of saphan-khwai and ari. The app's own neighbours list is ['ari','saphan-khwai']; named venues sit on both sides of the Phahonyothin centerline inside it (Dumbo, Honest Mistake, BRUT, Villa Market, Prasanmit and Vimut hospitals), while Big C, Lotus's, La Villa, Villa Supermarket, Maple Bear school and the Phyathai Phahonyothin hospital fall inside the 800 m circle but outside the polygon, in adjacent cells.

geography.notes: Polygon from app station-geometry.json; inside/outside checks computed by point-in-polygon against that polygon; area re-computed at 1.25 km² vs app 1.26.

temporal_scope.observed_period: Static geometry of the app snapshot
temporal_scope.notes: The brief's clipping hypothesis (extension stations to south/north) is contradicted; the actual clippers are the adjacent old-line cells.

evidence.paraphrase: App polygon is the 10-vertex cell with bbox lat 13.78068-13.79184, lng 100.53953-100.55426; area_km2 fact 1.26; neighbours ari and saphan-khwai.

evidence.locator: Overpass queries 1 and 4 — station and amenity coordinates
evidence.paraphrase: OSM coordinates for the named venues confirm which fall inside the polygon (Dumbo 13.78877,100.54803 in; Big C 13.79129,100.54953 out; La Villa 13.77986,100.5452 out).

limitations: Polygon vertex count and clipping are the coordinator's geometry checks to confirm independently (check_geometry.py).
'Inside the 800 m circle but outside the polygon' items are counted by the app's fact pipeline for some scores — flagged in open_issues.

claims.text_en: The app's district attribution 'phaya-thai 100%' checks out at district level: every one of 2,281 grid points sampled inside the app polygon falls within เขตพญาไท (Phaya Thai district) per OSM administrative boundary polygons; the Chatuchak district line passes just north of the polygon around Saphan Khwai, so the straddle the brief suspected does not exist at district level. Within Phaya Thai, however, the unit straddles two khwaengs — แขวงพญาไท (Phaya Thai subdistrict) takes about 51% of sampled points and แขวงสามเสนใน (Sam Sen Nai) about 49% — so the east-west split runs down the middle of the cell.

geography.notes: Grid share computed at 60x60 sampling over the polygon bbox; khwaeng shares at 50x50.

temporal_scope.observed_period: Boundaries as mapped in OSM (stable administrative lines)
temporal_scope.notes: The brief asked for a Phaya Thai/Chatuchak straddle check: verdict is no district straddle, but a near-half khwaeng straddle inside Phaya Thai.

evidence.locator: Overpass queries 6f/6g — เขตพญาไท, เขตจตุจักร, แขวงพญาไท, แขวงสามเสนใน, แขวงทุ่งพญาไท polygons (out geom) + point-in-polygon grids
evidence.paraphrase: Point-in-polygon testing of sampled grid points: 2,281/2,281 inside เขตพญาไท, 0 inside เขตจตุจักร; khwaeng split 811 points แขวงพญาไท vs 776 points แขวงสามเสนใน.

limitations: Estimate is sampling-based (roughly ±1-2 pp at this grid density).
OSM lacks a khwaeng relation named แขวงพหลโยธิน (queried); the mapped khwaeng set near the cell is what the split rests on.
A Thai-language search result independently described Soi Sena Ruam as being in แขวงสามเสนใน (snippet-only), consistent with the mapped split.

claims.text_en: The unit contains no rail station, and its transport-8 score rests on an app model that treats the phantom point as an operating stop: the app publishes resident/visitor transit times (7 min to Mo Chit, 13 to Siam) computed from a station that OSM and Thai Wikipedia agree does not exist. Nearest operating BTS stations are outside the polygon — Ari 734 m and Saphan Khwai 929 m in straight line. Surface transport runs on the main road only: OSM maps about 20 bus stops within 800 m along Phahonyothin (named stops include the Ari exit stops, 'Sutthisan Winitchai' to the east and 'Salirathavibhaga'), and Time Out notes buses stopping on Phahonyothin near La Villa and beneath Ari station. No boat piers (app fact: piers 0); the river is kilometres away.

geography.notes: Distances are straight-line OSM computations; no walking durations asserted.

temporal_scope.notes: The brief's transport question is answered mostly in the negative: 'BTS-only' is not even true — the unit is BTS-less.

evidence.locator: Overpass queries 1 (stations) and 7 (bus stops/platforms within 800 m)

No guide covers the scored unit as a station area — unsurprising, since no station exists there. Coverage breadth for the soi is thin but non-zero, and coverage breadth says nothing about actual popularity either way.

question_answers.question: Identity/scope: what exactly is this unit, which station anchors it, how is it clipped, and does it straddle districts?
question_answers.answer: The unit is the app's 'Sena Ruam' cell — but its namesake station does not exist. The anchor point (13.78594, 100.54686) is the site reserved for planned BTS infill station Sena Ruam (N6) between Ari (N5) and Saphan Khwai (N7) on Phahonyothin Road, never built; the app models it as an operating Sukhumvit Line station and its neighbours are 'ari' and 'saphan-khwai', not the brief's hypothesised 'phahonyothin-24'/'kasetsart-university' (4.7 km and 7.1 km away). The 1.25 km² cell is an 800 m circle clipped north/south by those two adjacent cells. District: 100% Phaya Thai per OSM boundaries (Chatuchak starts just north at Saphan Khwai), but split about 51/49 between the Phaya Thai and Sam Sen Nai khwaengs.
limitations: The brief's premises (operating extension station, extension-station clipping, Dec 2019-Dec 2020 phases for a Sena Ruam) are each contradicted; corrections carry sources.

question_answers.question: Everyday experience: mid-ring family living and commuter rhythm — what is it actually like?
question_answers.answer: A quiet, low-rise residential side-soi grid (Soi Sena Ruam = Phahon Yothin Soi 11) flanking a busy primary road. Guides describe cafe-lined quiet sois ('could be the new Ari', 2018; 'quiet residential sois shaded from the heat', 2026); daily anchors sit on the main road (two private hospitals at 149 m and 310 m; Villa Market 310 m; Big C and Lotus's at the 800 m edges; La Villa 700 m south). Commuter rhythm runs on Phahonyothin buses and by foot to BTS Ari or Saphan Khwai, both outside the cell (734 m / 929 m). No fresh market inside the cell (app markets: 0).
limitations: Resident voices unavailable (Reddit/TripAdvisor blocked per task); experience reads through editorial guides and map data.

question_answers.question: Values and mechanisms: what drives the high scores here?
question_answers.answer: Nightlife 9 is strip spillover: the Ari-Saphan Khwai bar-cafe corridor runs through the cell (Dumbo 339 m, Honest Mistake 323 m, BRUT 545 m inside; HOBS and O'Glee at the Ari edge), documented by guides since 2018 — not a Kasetsart student strip (7 km north). Food 8 rides the same strip (84 restaurants, 38 cafes mapped within 800 m). Daily-essentials 8 rides edge-clustered retail plus hospital frontage. Green 8 rests on the single 1.95 ha PRD public park at the cell's south-west margin. Transport 8 rests on an app model that assumes the unbuilt station exists.
limitations: The Overture mix behind nightlife 49 could not be decomposed; OSM maps only 11 bars.

question_answers.question: Counter-evidence: what contradicts the app's calm, high-scoring portrait?
question_answers.answer: Four counters: (1) no station inside the cell and a fare table that still charges for the missing one — the 1.6 km Saphan Khwai-Ari hop costs 25 baht, called out in the Bangkok Metropolitan Council on 4 Nov 2026; (2) the promised station has been unbuilt since 1999, i.e. the transport upside is a 27-year-old promise with no committed schedule; (3) the 26 Sep 2026 flood brought army detachments to the Phahonyothin/Ari frontage to clear flood-damaged vehicles, with the Saphan Khwai-Soi Ari 11 stretch on deep-standing-water lists; (4) the property-portal guide lists no cons at all (pro-bias) and admits it has no live listings, so its 2-bed floor above the app's blend is soft evidence, not proof.
limitations: Flood detail beyond the army deployment rests on snippet-only traffic alerts; the fare figure is a councilor's statement.

question_answers.question: Rhythm: how does the area change through the day?
question_answers.answer: Daytime is medical-and-commuter: hospital traffic at Prasanmit and Vimut on the frontage, buses along Phahonyothin, soi cafes serving workers (the pattern BK profiled in 2018). Evenings import the crowd: the mapped bars draw the Ari-Saphan Khwai strip's customers while the soi itself stays residential. The main road can shut down abruptly in monsoon downpours, as September 2026 showed.
limitations: No hour-by-hour source; rhythm inferred from venue types and guide framing.

question_answers.question: Walkability: station entrances, Phahonyothin sidewalks vs sois — measured how?
question_answers.answer: Measured in straight-line distances, not durations: BTS Ari 734 m and Saphan Khwai 929 m from the center, both outside the cell; on-cell anchors at 149-700 m. BK Magazine praised the soi's fresh tactile paving as stroll-friendly (2018); Time Out describes the wider area's walkable side-sois. The main road is a traffic-heavy primary corridor (bus stops every few hundred metres; army deployed to it during the 2026 flood). No entrance-level detail exists for a station that was never built.
limitations: No radius-to-time conversion used or implied; sidewalk-condition sourcing is limited to the two editorial guides.

question_answers.question: Daily life: markets, groceries, hospitals, schools?
question_answers.answer: Hospitals are the standout: Prasanmit (149 m, the planned station's frontage hospital), Vimut (310 m, opened 2021), Phyathai Phahonyothin (769 m). Groceries: Villa Market 310 m in-cell; Big C 661 m and Lotus's 678 m at the circle's edges; La Villa community mall 700 m south with Villa Supermarket beside it. No fresh market inside the cell (app markets: 0; one unnamed OSM marketplace 650 m SSW outside the polygon). Schools: Maple Bear International 665 m and รุจิเสรีวิทยา 703 m. The app counts 100 essentials and 12 convenience stores in the cell.
limitations: The unnamed marketplace could not be identified; individual convenience chains not listed.

question_answers.question: Affordability: district blend vs the unit's own stock; asking vs signed?
question_answers.answer: The app's 18,000/37,000 is a Phaya Thai district blend (editorial, typical_asking, updated 2026-09), not this cell's market. The nearest corridor guide (BAANLYY Saphan Khwai, 2026-07-01) gives indicative 1-bed 20,000-38,000 and 2-bed 38,000-72,000 with no live listings behind it. Read against that, the 1-bed blend is plausible-to-slightly-optimistic and the 2-bed 37,000 sits at or below the guide's floor — the rent-7 'moderate' rating leans optimistic for two-bedrooms on this corridor. Asking-vs-signed spread for the unit's own stock is unknown.
limitations: No Sena Ruam-specific rent series found; portal data indicative only.

question_answers.question: Green/quiet: what is the 1.8 ha park, and is the buffer honest?
question_answers.answer: The park is สวนสาธารณะกรมประชาสัมพันธ์ — the Public Relations Department public park, a compound park on Phahonyothin Road, mapped by OSM at about 1.95 ha (app: 1.8 ha). Buffer honesty: its centroid is 871 m south-west of the center — outside the scored polygon, catching the 800 m circle's edge — so the green score rests on one edge park, not a park system; the remaining mapped green is unnamed garden polygons. Quiet is well supported by the soi texture guides describe, but the 2026 flood event is the counterpoint to an unqualified calm reading.
limitations: Park's public access hours unverified; app-vs-OSM hectare difference unexplained.

question_answers.question: Conditional fit: who does this cell actually suit?
question_answers.answer: Fits: hospital workers and patients (two private hospitals on the frontage); renters priced out of Ari proper who want the same cafe-soi texture at corridor prices; bus-and-shophouse commuters whose day runs along Phahonyothin. Poor fit: anyone choosing the cell for BTS at the door — the stations are 734 m and 929 m away in other cells and the fare table punishes the gap; and buyers of the 'station area' label itself, since the station is a 27-year-old plan. Families get quiet sois and schools at 665-703 m but should weigh flood exposure on the main road.
limitations: Fit statements are researcher synthesis over the sourced claims, not survey data.

question_answers.question: Recent changes 2024-2026: extension effects, construction, news?
question_answers.answer: Three dated items: (1) 4 Nov 2026 — the Bangkok Metropolitan Council again took up the unbuilt Sena Ruam station (in plan since 1999), with BMA committing only to coordinate ahead of the 2029 concession handover and pledging fare unification under MRTA; (2) 26 Sep 2026 — corridor flooding with army deployment on the Phahonyothin/Ari frontage; (3) 2024-2026 editorial: Time Out's Ari guide (30 May 2026) and BAANLYY's Saphan Khwai guide (1 Jul 2026) re-frame the strip under the neighbouring nodes' names, while the soi's own 2018 guide remains its latest dedicated coverage. No construction has started at the N6 site.
limitations: The extension's effects (2019-2020 openings) pre-date the 2024-2026 window; no 2024-2026 construction news exists to report.

question_answers.question: Uncertainties and outside-the-score factors, including the nightlife-9 mechanism?
question_answers.answer: Open items: the 49-venue nightlife count could not be decomposed (OSM: 11 named bars; the mechanism is best read as Ari-Saphan Khwai strip spillover); the app's rent blend vs the corridor guide's higher 2-bed floor; the PRD park's centroid outside the polygon and its public-access status; the app's transit model treating a phantom station as real; unlinked flood-scale reports; bus route numbers unsourced; and the N6 project's genuinely open status (infobox says start 2026/service 2032, the same page's history says cancelled, BMA says 'will coordinate'). See open_issues OI-1 to OI-8.
limitations: Uncertainty inventory bounded by this session's tools (Reddit/TripAdvisor/Bangkok Post not accessible).

editorial.preview: The app's 'Sena Ruam' is not a place the BTS map recognizes: the scored cell is the quiet, cafe-lined gap between Ari and Saphan Khwai on Phahonyothin Road — 734 m and 929 m from the nearest stations — named for a soi whose own 2018 guide noted the 'grayed-out station' that was supposed to rise here and never did.
editorial.guide_lead: Soi Sena Ruam — officially Phahon Yothin Soi 11 — is a residential side-soi grid in Phaya Thai strung along the Phahonyothin corridor: two private hospitals and a compound park at the edges, Villa Market and La Villa within 700 m, craft bars spilling in from the Ari end, and a BTS station that has been 'coming' since 1999 and still adds 25 baht to the fare table in 2026.

strengths.text: Everyday completeness at short distances: Prasanmit hospital about 149 m and Vimut about 310 m on the road frontage, Villa Market at 310 m, Big C and Lotus's within the 800 m sweep, and 100 essentials counted inside the cell.

A documented cafe-and-bar strip instead of a nightlife district: the Ari-Saphan Khwai corridor carries the venues behind nightlife 9 — Dumbo, Honest Mistake and BRUT map inside the cell — while BAANLYY scores Saphan Khwai nightlife 8/10 and Time Out lists Ari's low-lit bars.

Low-rise residential texture with a published identity: BK Magazine's 2018 soi guide ('could be the new Ari') and Time Out's 'quiet residential sois shaded from the heat' match the grid the app scores.
Clean district math: the cell sits entirely in Phaya Thai — Chatuchak starts just north at Saphan Khwai — split roughly half-and-half between the Phaya Thai and Sam Sen Nai khwaengs.

tradeoffs.text: There is no station. BTS Ari is 734 m and Saphan Khwai 929 m away, both in other cells; transport 8 rests on an app model that treats the unbuilt N6 'Sena Ruam' as an operating stop.

The missing station still costs money: BTSC's fare table counts N6, so the 1.6 km Saphan Khwai-Ari hop runs 25 baht — called out in the Bangkok Metropolitan Council in November 2026 as more than longer extension hops.
Green is thin and off-center: the only named park (the Public Relations Department public park, about 1.95 ha mapped) sits at the cell's south-west margin, its centroid 871 m from the center.
September 2026 flooding hit this Phahonyothin stretch hard enough to bring in army detachments to clear flood-damaged vehicles — a live risk no score input carries.

day_night.text: Daytime rhythm is medical and commuter: hospital traffic at Prasanmit and Vimut, buses along Phahonyothin, and the soi cafes that served office workers when BK Magazine profiled the street in 2018.
Evenings import their crowd: the mapped bars (Dumbo 339 m, Honest Mistake 323 m, BRUT 545 m) draw the Ari-Saphan Khwai strip's customers while the soi itself stays residential.

Weekends read cafe-first: the soi's four 2018-era independent cafes (Caffe Undici, Doctor Roaster, PH1b, Before Thirtieth) set the register; only the attached hotel's survival (Craftsman Bangkok) is corroborated for 2026.
When the trains are far away, the corridor is bus-and-road territory — and the September 2026 flood showed how quickly the main road can stop.

within_area_variation.text: East of Phahonyothin (Sam Sen Nai khwaeng side): the hospital frontage, Vimut, the school and a denser shophouse grid — close to half the cell.
West of Phahonyothin (Phaya Thai khwaeng side): the Soi Sena Ruam cafe grid and, at the far margin, the Public Relations Department park.
The south-west corner thins toward La Villa and Ari's cell boundary; the north edge runs to Saphan Khwai's retail, with Big C and Lotus's just outside the polygon.
The center point itself — where the N6 station would have risen in front of Prasanmit — is the cell's transit dead center: no station, no square, just the primary road.

conditional_fit.text: Fits: hospital workers and patients, renters priced out of Ari proper who want the same cafe-soi texture at corridor rents, and anyone whose day runs along Phahonyothin by bus.
Poor fit: anyone choosing this cell for BTS at the door — the stations are outside it, the fare table charges for the gap, and the promised station has no schedule.
Families get the quiet-soi logic (schools at 665-703 m, low-rise housing) but should weigh the 2026 flood record on the main road against it.

uncertainties.text: The 49-venue nightlife count (Overture) could not be decomposed; OSM maps 11 named bars, so whatever sits behind the difference (shophouse pubs, lounges, karaokes) is unverified.
The app's rent figures are a district blend; BAANLYY's indicative 2-bed floor (38,000) sits above the blend's 37,000, and no signed-rent data exists for the cell's own stock.
The Public Relations Department park's public-access status and hours were not verified, and its centroid lies outside the scored polygon.
BK Magazine's 2018 venue list may be partly stale; only Craftsman Bangkok's survival is corroborated for 2026.
Bus route numbers serving the soi-mouth stops were not sourced, and khlong-boat access was not checked (app fact: piers 0).

Whether N6 construction ever starts is genuinely open: the infobox says construction expected 2026 and service 2032, the same article's history says cancelled, and the BMA said in November 2026 only that it will coordinate.

open_issues.issue: App models the unbuilt planned station N6 'Sena Ruam' as an operating bts_sukhumvit station (rail.json), which anchors transport 8, transit_minutes and the area's very identity.
open_issues.notes: Coordinator decision needed: flag, rename (e.g. 'soi-sena-ruam'), or re-point the area. OSM + Thai Wikipedia + Prachachat (2026-11-05) all confirm the station does not exist; BTS's fare table still includes it (25-baht Saphan Khwai-Ari anomaly).
